data.title: The Person Beside Me
data.excerpt: The journey lasted only two hours, but a conversation with the stranger beside him changed something inside him.
content: The train was almost empty when Evan boarded.
He took the window seat and spent the first twenty minutes staring at the passing fields.
At the next station, an old man sat beside him.
They talked about small things at first: the weather, the train, the town they were leaving behind.
Eventually, Evan told the stranger that he was going home because he had lost his job and did not know what came next.
The old man listened without interrupting.
Before getting off, he handed Evan a folded piece of paper.
"You don't need to know what comes next," he said. "You only need to know where you're getting off."
Evan unfolded the paper after the doors closed.
"A wrong turn is still a direction."
Evan looked out the window again.
For the first time that day, he wasn't afraid of the journey home.
